newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch moot "Marshall Plan" for East Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dutch moot "Marshall Plan" for East Europe.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Wednesday Western Europe and its North American allies should join forces to back a new "Marshall Plan" to support the economic regeneration of Eastern Europe.

Kok, whose country currently holds the European Union presidency, made the remarks in a radio interview ahead of celebrations to mark the 50th anniversary of the original U.S. Marshall Plan to rebuild Europe's economy after World War Two.
U.S. President Bill Clinton will be among the European and North American leaders who will attend the event in The Hague.
Kok, who is expected to elaborate on his remarks in a speech later on Wednesday, said the Marshall Plan could not be copied wholesale but the underlying idea was still practicable.
He said he envisaged public and private sectors working together to support infrastructure projects in Eastern Europe.
"After all that brings people in the different parts of Europe together quite literally," he said.
Kok said a new Marshall Plan would hold out the prospect of greater prosperity for the people of Eastern Europe but would also be beneficial to the continent as a whole.
On the 50th anniversary of the original Marshall Plan it was "high time" for Europeans and North Americans to discuss a similar effort for Eastern Europe in concrete terms, he said.
Between 1948 and 1952, the United States gave more than $12 billion of aid to 16 European countries to help them rebuild their shattered industries and stave off hunger and disease.

Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin did not allow Marshall Aid to be distributed to Eastern Europe, where living standards fell far behind those in the West as the region remained under communist rule for almost half a century after the war.
